classification.difficultyReason: Find the isosceles cross-section area, extend to prism volume and convert cubic metres to litres.

content.prompt:
A dam is in the shape of a triangular prism which is $50\mathrm{\ m}$ long, as shown.
Both ends of the dam, $ABC$ and $DEF$, are isosceles triangles with equal sides of 25 metres.
The included angles $\angle BAC$ and $\angle EDF$ are each $150^\circ$
Calculate the number of litres of water the dam will hold when full.

spec.description: Wide oblique triangular prism, with front end ABC and rear end DEF. A and D are the lower vertices. Matching ticks mark AB and AC; AB is labelled 25 m. The front interior angle at A is labelled 150°. BE is labelled 50 m. Front end and the exposed upper portion of the rear end have light stippling. ED disappears behind the longitudinal face where its projection intersects CF; that crossing is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=DE=DF=25 m; angle BAC=angle EDF=150 degrees; longitudinal edges AD, BE and CF represent 50 m. Perspective projection follows the source and does not display the true cross-section angle.
